text:
- No `apps/api/src/db/pool.ts` exposes a `pg.Pool` configured for the Postgres 16 `tstzrange` / `EXCLUDE USING gist` workload (e.g., `application_name`, statement timeout, `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout`); the spec calls out Postgres 16 as a non-negotiable primitive, but the pool has no knobs that prove the engine will tolerate booking-time transactions.
- No `pgcrypto` / `uuid-ossp` extension is enabled in `0001_init_bootstrap.sql`; the migration uses `gen_random_uuid()` and comments mention `pgcrypto`, but the extension is never created — first-run against a fresh DB will fail with "function gen_random_uuid() does not exist".
- The migration lacks an `updated_at` column / trigger on the entities, but the architecture implies mutable rows; E0-S2 widening will need to retrofit timestamps and there is no shared `now()` discipline documented at E0-S1.
- No `index` on `branch(clinic_id)` even though every branch lookup joins on it; a future `branch` → `clinic` query will table-scan.
- No `index` on `doctor_branch(branch_id)` for the inverse lookup that "receptionist at branch X sees doctors" requires; only `(doctor_id, branch_id)` PK is present.
- No `index` on `patient(phone_number)` beyond the implicit UNIQUE; Postgres still needs the explicit B-tree for hash-join plans, and the architecture expects server-side phone filtering to be hot.
- `receptionist` and `admin_user` have no `branch_ids`-like scoping column or unique constraint that makes the seed idempotent without the `WHERE NOT EXISTS` hack — the seed uses string-name uniqueness instead of a stable identifier, so renaming a receptionist silently duplicates the row.
- The `seed` script does not snapshot row counts as the spec acceptance requires (`first run snapshots row counts; second run asserts equality`); `seed.test.ts` only checks for the keywords in source, never actually runs the seed twice and compares counts.
- `seed.test.ts` does not actually invoke `seed()` against a Postgres — the test asserts source-level invariants only; a developer expecting CI to assert row-count equality gets false confidence.
- No `apps/api/test/auth.test.ts` exists — the spec calls out that E0-S1's auth middleware must already accept the claim envelope, but there is no test asserting that `x-auth-claim` with `role=doctor` populates `req.auth.claim`, that `branch_ids=[]` returns 403, that body fields are never trusted, or that patient tokens with empty `branch_ids` are allowed.
- The body-never-trusted rule is documented in a comment but not asserted by any test; an attacker who POSTs `{role:"admin", branch_ids:["x"]}` could bypass silently because the middleware only reads headers.
- No test asserts that `patient` cannot authenticate through staff routes and vice versa (architecture §3.1 cross-role boundary); the `authMiddleware` accepts any role from the header.
- The `x-auth-claim` header is a debug surface, not a real token — production exposure of `req.header('x-auth-claim')` means any client can mint an admin claim by setting a header; the comment acknowledges E0-S3 will replace it, but no kill-switch exists for non-dev environments.
- No CORS configuration in `apps/api/src/app.ts`; the patient web at `:5173` calling the API at `:3001` will be blocked unless CORS is added later — the spec mentions "Edge / API gateway (auth, rate-limit, tz normalization, CORS)" in §2 component map.
- No rate-limit middleware on `/patient/otp/send` (or anywhere) — the SMS OTP gateway must enforce 3-attempt cap per 10-minute window; even though E0-S4 owns the gateway, the API layer's rate-limit posture is unestablished at E0-S1.
- No request-body size limit enforcement on `express.json({ limit: '64kb' })` is paired with content-type validation; an attacker can send `Content-Type: application/json` with a 10MB body bypassing `limit` via `application/octet-stream` (Express only limits on `json` middleware) — minor, but worth flagging.
- `requestLogger` is mounted before `initLogContext` in `app.ts`, but `initLogContext` is a no-op pass-through; the `customProps` reads `(req as ...).logCtx` directly, so any race where a handler logs before `attachLogContext` runs yields a stale `null` — the contract says `actor_role` etc. are always present, but no test asserts they default to `null` rather than `undefined`.
- The structured-log test in `log.test.ts` does NOT exercise the actual `requestLogger` middleware from `middleware/log.ts`; it constructs a standalone pino instance with the same redact paths but the production code uses `pino-http` which adds `req`/`res` objects that change the redact path semantics. The test would not catch a regression where the real middleware drops a field.
- No test asserts that `appointment_id` is `null` (not `undefined`) in the log envelope when not in scope; downstream log consumers depending on JSON shape consistency could break.
- The `redactPaths` list covers `req.body.password`, `req.body.phone_number`, `req.body.code`, but not `req.body.phone` (which is what many APIs use), `req.body.email`, or `req.body.token`; the comment says "phone_number" but the spec mentions OTP `code` and PII phone, and the E0-S4 OTP gateway will emit these under other key names.
- No test asserts that `phone_number` redact survives deeper paths (the comment notes "pino redact only walks the exact paths listed. We list the dotted paths the API surface actually emits today"); there is no enforcement that future code cannot introduce `user.phone` or `patient.phone` fields that bypass redaction.
- The pino `redact` paths do not include `req.headers.authorization` for `Bearer` tokens that E0-S3 will introduce — the diff adds `req.headers.authorization` to the list, but `x-auth-claim` itself (which carries role/branches) is NOT in the redact list; the entire claim envelope will be serialized into logs as `req.headers["x-auth-claim"]`, leaking the role and branch list to log storage.
- `apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts` sets `x-auth-claim` parsing but does NOT add `x-auth-claim` to the pino redact list; the auth claim containing `branch_ids` will land in log lines verbatim.
- `pg.Pool.on('error', ...)` uses `console.error` instead of the structured `logger`, so idle-client errors skip the structured-log contract; the spec says "every log line carries `request_id`...".
- The double-booking counter that "MUST remain 0" per architecture §6 is not seeded in `NAMED_COUNTERS`; downstream stories will need to add it but the contract is binding.
- No `trace_id` field on structured logs; architecture §6 explicitly lists `trace_id` alongside `actor_role`, `actor_id`, `appointment_id` as fields structured logs include. The four-field contract in `log.test.ts` matches the spec's "four fields", but the architecture's §6 adds `trace_id` and that field is absent from both the implementation and the test.
- No `index.ts` re-exports for `apps/api/src/types/auth.ts` and `apps/api/src/types/health.ts`; the spec says "Web app imports via relative path for now" but there is no documented import path from `apps/web` to these types — `apps/web/package.json` has no dependency on `@clinic/api` and no path mapping, so the claim "Web app imports via relative path" is impossible without that wiring.
- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` declares `packages/*` but no `packages/` directory exists; `pnpm -r` will succeed but the workspace declaration anticipates a third consumer the E0-S1 spec says is deferred until "a third consumer appears" — fine as-is, but no shared-types package placeholder means E0-S3 will need to create one without prior scaffolding.
- `apps/api/package.json` `db:migrate` script references `dist/db/migrations/.applied.json` but the build step is `tsc -p tsconfig.json` which won't run the `node-pg-migrate` JS runner; the migration runner path points at compiled output but `tsc` doesn't run `node-pg-migrate`'s build step. The first run after `pnpm build` will fail because `dist/` won't exist or `.applied.json` won't be there.
- `node-pg-migrate` is invoked with `-m db/migrations` but the migrations live under `apps/api/db/migrations`; from the api package root that path is correct, but `pnpm -w db:migrate` filters to `@clinic/api` and runs from there — fine, but the README/spec mentions `pnpm -w db:migrate` (workspace root) which would resolve `db/migrations` relative to the wrong directory.
- `apps/api/db/seeds/01_minimum.ts` uses `client.query` with the type parameter `query<{ id: string }>(...)` but then does `client.query('BEGIN')` without generic — minor, but the seed's `RETURNING id` for `clinic` uses `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id`, which on a no-op insert returns zero rows, forcing the second `SELECT` round-trip; a `WITH ... INSERT ... SELECT` pattern would be cleaner.
- The seed creates no `clinic_name` UNIQUE constraint, so `clinic.name` lookup-by-name is the idempotency anchor — renaming a clinic between seed runs would silently create a duplicate; the spec promises "Running this twice produces identical row counts" but the column has no UNIQUE constraint enforcing that.
- `branch` has no UNIQUE on `(clinic_id, name)` either; same rename-breaks-idempotency problem.
- `doctor.full_name` has no UNIQUE constraint; the seed's `WHERE NOT EXISTS` check is the only thing preventing duplicates.
- `receptionist(branch_id, full_name)` has no UNIQUE constraint; the seed's `WHERE NOT EXISTS` is the only protection.
- `admin_user.full_name` has no UNIQUE constraint; same.
- The migration creates `branch.tz DEFAULT 'UTC'` but the architecture §4 says `Branch.tz` is REQUIRED for production — `DEFAULT 'UTC'` means a developer can leave it blank and the seed uses `'UTC'` for `BRANCH_TZ`; the spec expects IANA timezones, and `'UTC'` is technically valid IANA, but the spec for S5 expects distinct time zones across branches and there is no validation that the value parses as IANA.
- `apps/api/src/db/pool.ts` `pingDb()` swallows ALL errors and returns `false`, masking real connection errors (auth failure, SSL failure) as "unreachable" — a developer with bad credentials will see `/readyz` returning 503 with no diagnostic in the log.
- `apps/api/src/server.ts` calls `app.listen(PORT, ...)` but does not handle `listen` errors (e.g., EADDRINUSE); a port collision crashes the process with no retry — minor, but the spec acceptance says "the process starts" even on DB-down; port collision is symmetric.
- The CI workflow does not cache `node_modules` between runs despite using `pnpm/action-setup` with `cache: 'pnpm'` for setup-node; the setup-node `cache: pnpm` integration requires a separate `cache` step (or the action does cache) — the `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile=false` flag is suspicious: frozen lockfile is the right choice for CI to prevent drift.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile=false` is wrong for CI; the spec says "CI must run lint + unit tests on every push" implying a deterministic install; `--frozen-lockfile=false` allows the lockfile to mutate in CI, which means a feature branch can introduce a lockfile change that fails the main branch.
- No `pnpm-lock.yaml` is in the diff (correct — pnpm generates it on first install), but no `.npmrc` workspace-level file declares the `node-version` for engines; engines is in `package.json` but not enforced by pnpm in CI.
- No `package.json` for `apps/web` includes a `prepare` or `postinstall` hook for vite to warm up; trivial, but the spec calls for `pnpm dev` to bring both up — `pnpm -r --parallel --stream run dev` from root will, but each package's `dev` runs independently and there's no orchestration guarantee.
- The `Makefile` `clean` target removes `node_modules` but not `dist`, `.turbo`, `coverage`, or `*.tsbuildinfo`; a stale build artifact can poison the next `pnpm -w typecheck` since `--noEmit` skips emit but `tsc -p tsconfig.json` in the build script emits to `dist/`.
- The CI workflow does not run on `pull_request` for forks (it does, but with `actions/checkout@v4` no `persist-credentials: false`); minor, but a fork PR could exfiltrate tokens via workflow — orthogonal to the spec but a security note for CI hardening.
- No `dependabot.yml` / `renovate.json` — pnpm lockfile + pinned versions in package.json will rot; spec implies CI green on a clean commit but doesn't address dependency updates.
- No `README.md` for the repo; the spec promises "One command brings the stack up: `pnpm dev` (or `make dev` alias)" but a first-time developer needs a README explaining Postgres requirement, env setup, and how to seed.
- No `LICENSE`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, or `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` — minor, but the spec implies a real platform.
- No `.editorconfig` — pnpm workspace + multiple editors will produce inconsistent formatting.
- No `.prettierrc` / `.prettierignore` — the placeholder CSS in `tokens.css` uses mixed spacing (e.g., `0 0 0 3px rgba(...)` vs `0 1px 2px rgba(...)`); style drift across contributors is guaranteed.
- `apps/web/src/main.tsx` imports `./styles/tokens.css` and `index.html` `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/src/styles/tokens.css" />` — double-loading the stylesheet (Vite resolves the same path twice); harmless but wasteful.
- `tokens.css` defines `--brand-primary-dark: #2dd4bf` (a teal) and the spec §7 says "Status pills never use brand teal"; this token's name suggests a teal usage pattern that the placeholder might use for status pills. No test or lint enforces this in E0-S1.
- `tokens.css` includes a `transition: color 120ms ease;` on `.placeholder__heading`; the spec says "no transitions on the placeholder" under reduced motion but the transition exists in the default state — the design check for `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes them, but DevTools inspection in default mode will show a transition, which a reviewer might flag against "zero layout shift" semantics.
- The `index.html` `<title>` is hard-coded English; no `<meta name="description">` or i18n hooks — minimal for E0-S1 but the architecture §3 expects IANA tz and design tokens to be the single source; title drift is unguarded.
- `apps/web/src/App.tsx` is a function but is exported as `App` while `main.tsx` uses named import `{ App }`; this works but the export style is inconsistent with the rest of the API which uses `export function` — minor consistency note.
- No `index.html` favicon — 404 in DevTools network tab; reviewer blocker for "no web font requests" but not for favicon.
- `apps/api/src/app.ts` does not trust-proxy configuration; behind a load balancer, `req.ip` and the `x-request-id` header would be attacker-controlled. Architecture §2 mentions an "Edge / API gateway (auth, rate-limit, tz normalization, CORS)" — no `app.set('trust proxy', ...)` means the gateway pattern is incomplete.
- No `helmet` middleware for security headers; spec doesn't require it but the architecture §6 implicit security posture suggests it.
- `apps/api/src/middleware/log.ts` `customLogLevel` returns `'warn'` for 4xx but never logs the response body; a 4xx with PII in the response (e.g., validation error echoing phone) would not be captured.
- `apps/api/src/middleware/log.ts` `customProps` always emits `actor_role: null, actor_id: null, appointment_id: null` for unauthenticated requests; the spec says "every log line carries `request_id`, `actor_role`, `actor_id`, `appointment_id` when in scope" — `null` is honest but a log consumer expecting absence of the key (e.g., grep-based search) will get false negatives.
- The auth middleware attaches `actor_role` and `actor_id` via `attachLogContext`, but `appointment_id` is never attached by E0-S1 code; the test asserts the field is present in captured log lines only when the test manually constructs the context — no production code path attaches `appointment_id` yet. The acceptance criterion ("when the structured-log middleware emits a line within scope of an appointment, then the captured JSON contains `appointment_id`") has no exercised production code path in this diff.
- `apps/api/test/health.test.ts` mutates `process.env` globally and restores it via `process.env = prev`; this is unsafe in `node:test` because other tests can run concurrently and observe the mutated env. A more idiomatic pattern is to set per-test and restore in `finally` (it does), but the test runner may share state.
- The `health.test.ts` test relies on `127.0.0.1:1` being closed; on some CI environments, port 1 may be filtered or unreachable for non-network reasons (e.g., seccomp). A more reliable pattern is `127.0.0.1:0` plus a closed server, or a mock at the `pg.Pool` level.
- The `log.test.ts` test passes but never asserts that the production `pino` instance (from `middleware/log.ts`) emits fields with the expected names; the test re-creates a fresh pino instance, decoupling the test from production behavior.
- The `seed.test.ts` regex `assert.match(src, /INSERT INTO clinic/)` would also match `INSERT INTO clinic_x` or a comment; no anchoring.
- `seed.test.ts` does not assert that the seed handles a database where the tables don't exist; `01_minimum.ts` will throw on missing tables, but `seed.test.ts` doesn't exercise that path — fine for source-level check, but a CI test against a real DB would catch this.
- `apps/api/test/log.test.ts` does not assert that `requestLogger` (the production middleware) emits `request_id` in the log line — it only asserts a hand-built pino instance emits the field. The integration is untested.
- The `apps/api/test/health.test.ts` does not cover `200 /readyz` against a live DB; only the 503 path is covered. Acceptance criterion "with DB up" is not asserted.
- No `apps/web` build artifacts or preview script test; the CI build step (`pnpm -w build`) will run `vite build` but no test asserts the dist HTML loads.
- No `apps/web/src/App.tsx` test using `@testing-library/react` (or similar); the spec doesn't require it, but E0-S1 is a "runnable skeleton" and a smoke test for the placeholder would catch a broken `var(--brand-primary)` reference.
- The diff has no `Dockerfile` / `docker-compose.yml`; spec says "No Docker in this story (deferred — `pg` connection string is read from env so Docker can be added later without re-platforming)". Fine.
- The diff has no `apps/api/src/middleware/error.ts` to convert errors to a canonical `ErrorEnvelope` (`{code, what, why, can_do, details}`); the architecture §5 + AD-4 mandate the envelope but the only error handler in `app.ts` returns `{ error: 'internal_error' }` — not the canonical shape. E0-S1 doesn't need full envelopes but a stub or TODO pointing to where it will land would help.
- The metrics endpoint `/metrics` returns plain JSON `{ counters: ... }`; the architecture §9 ADR mentions Prometheus for observability; E0-S6 will swap to Prometheus exposition format, but no migration plan or feature flag exists.
- The metrics endpoint is publicly accessible; no auth, no rate-limit; the architecture doesn't require auth on `/metrics` but Prometheus convention often restricts it to internal scrapers — minor.
- No `apps/api/src/middleware/tz.ts` for tz normalization; architecture §6 / AD-9 say "Edge gateway normalizes incoming timestamps to UTC only, never to a tz" — E0-S1 doesn't ship the gateway, but no placeholder or contract note documents where it will sit.
- The `apps/api/src/app.ts` does not validate `req.body` against a schema (e.g., zod); the architecture AD-4 closed-enum `ErrorEnvelope.code` cannot be enforced without a validator at the API edge. E0-S1 doesn't ship endpoints, but the discipline is unestablished.
- The auth middleware `authMiddleware` always `next()`s (or 403s); it does not differentiate routes that REQUIRE auth from routes that allow anonymous — E0-S3 will need a `requireAuth(role)` decorator and the middleware has no hooks for that.
- The `apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts` `parseClaimHeader` does NOT verify the claim is signed; the architecture §3.1 says "session tokens must carry `{role, branch_ids, scope, doctor_id?}` plus a refresh contract" — a "session token" implies signing. The stub's documentation acknowledges this ("E0-S3 replaces this with a real provider"), but the absence of any signature check means anyone can mint an admin token. E0-S1 is dev-only, but a guard like `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') throw` would be a safety net.
- No `apps/api/test/auth.test.ts` asserts that a malformed `x-auth-claim` JSON yields anonymous (not crash); the spec implies "invalid shape yields anonymous context" but no test asserts that.
- No test asserts the `initLogContext` middleware does not throw; trivial.
- No test asserts the `/metrics` endpoint returns the named counters with value 0 on a fresh process; the spec says "empty counter registry seeded with the named counters" and acceptance implies `GET /metrics` is testable.
- No `apps/api/test/metrics.test.ts` exists; the named-counter contract is untested.
- No integration test for the `request_id` middleware round-trip; the spec says "request_id middleware attaches a UUID per request" but no test asserts a response carries the `x-request-id` header echoed from input.
- No test asserts the `x-request-id` response header is set; the production code does `res.setHeader('x-request-id', id)`, but no test reads it back.
- No `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `catalog:` block (pnpm 9+ feature) for shared versions; each package pins its own TypeScript and ESLint versions, which will drift over time.
- The `apps/api/src/middleware/log.ts` `cryptoRandom` uses `globalThis.crypto.randomUUID()`; fine on Node 20, but the codebase has no polyfill or guard for older Node — `engines` says `>=20.0.0` but the runtime check is absent.
- The pino redact list has no entry for `req.body.otp`, `req.body.otp_code`, `req.body.session_token`, `req.body.refresh_token`, or `req.body.password_reset` — patterns the E0-S3/S4 stories will introduce; pre-emptive coverage in E0-S1 would establish the discipline.
- No `apps/api/.env.test` or test-mode env file; the spec implies CI must run without a live DB, but `process.env` defaults could leak into tests (e.g., a developer's local `DATABASE_URL`).
- The CI workflow lacks a `concurrency:` block to cancel superseded runs; minor but standard hygiene.
- The CI workflow has no `permissions:` block restricting GITHUB_TOKEN scope; minor but standard hardening.
- The CI workflow uses `pnpm/action-setup@v4` with `version: 12` but no `packages/*` allow-build is declared in `.npmrc`; the pnpm-workspace.yaml has `allowBuilds: esbuild: true`, fine, but `.npmrc` lacks `node-linker=hoisted` or `shamefully-hoist=true` which may be needed for some Vite setups.
- The `apps/api/db/migrations/0001_init_bootstrap.sql` filename has no `node-pg-migrate`-style numeric suffix that the runner expects; the tool may require `1234567890_name.sql` or `123_name.sql` format depending on version.
- The `apps/api/package.json` `db:migrate` script uses `--env DATABASE_URL` which `node-pg-migrate` interprets as "look in the env file for `DATABASE_URL`", not "use the env var directly"; the correct flag is `--database-url-var DATABASE_URL` (newer versions) or `--envPath .env`. As written, the migration runner will look for `DATABASE_URL` in `.env`, not in `process.env`.
- The `apps/api/package.json` `db:migrate` script references `-f dist/db/migrations/.applied.json`; the migration runner would need the `dist/` to be built first (i.e., `pnpm build` must precede `db:migrate`); the `dev` script doesn't enforce this and the Makefile `db-migrate` target doesn't build.
- The Makefile `db-migrate` target calls `pnpm -w db:migrate` which filters to `@clinic/api`, then runs the package script — but the package script uses `node-pg-migrate` which expects JS migrations or SQL files; SQL files with `-j sql` should work, but the file path resolution from `apps/api` may differ.
- The seed script logs `seed_complete` on stdout but the structured-log contract says pino must emit this; `console.log` bypasses the request_id context — minor consistency issue.
- No `.dockerignore`; not in scope but related to "Docker can be added later without re-platforming".
- The `apps/api/.eslintrc.cjs` extends `eslint:recommended` and `@typescript-eslint/recommended` but no `import/order` or `import/no-unresolved`; the codebase uses `.js` extensions in relative imports (e.g., `from '../db/pool.js'`) which is correct for ESM but a lint rule would enforce it.
- The `apps/web/.eslintrc.cjs` doesn't extend `plugin:react/jsx-runtime` (only `plugin:react/recommended`) but disables `react/react-in-jsx-scope`; fine but inconsistent.
- The `apps/api/tsconfig.json` `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true` will surface indexing issues at compile time — good — but the test `seed.test.ts` uses `captured[0]!` non-null assertion; this is acceptable but worth noting.
- The `apps/web/tsconfig.json` doesn't extend a base config; `apps/api/tsconfig.json` doesn't either. A `tsconfig.base.json` at the root would enforce consistency.
- No `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `cleanup` or `onlyBuiltDependencies` for security; not required by spec but pnpm 9+ defaults.
- The `apps/api/src/types/auth.ts` `AuthClaim` type uses `branch_ids: string[]` but no brand type for UUIDs; a future story will need `Brand<string, 'BranchId'>` to prevent string-mixing bugs.
- The `apps/api/src/types/auth.ts` `Role` enum is missing `'staff'` as a parent role or future roles like `'nurse'`, `'manager'` — the architecture §4 RoleFieldPolicy implies future roles will be added and the policy must be declared at provisioning; the type is closed but no extensibility hook exists.
- The `apps/api/src/types/health.ts` `ReadyResponse` doesn't include `uptime` or `version`; spec doesn't require them but production readiness probes often want them.
- No `/api/v1` or versioning prefix on routes; E0-S1 ships `/healthz` and `/readyz` directly, but later stories adding `/bookings`, `/recurring/*` etc. will need versioning discipline.
- The CI workflow lacks `concurrency.cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.workflow_ref }}`; standard hygiene.
- The CI workflow's `actions/setup-node@v4` `cache: 'pnpm'` flag is deprecated; `pnpm/action-setup@v4` should handle caching, but the deprecated flag may emit warnings.
- The `apps/api/package.json` `test` script uses `node --import tsx --test test/*.test.ts` which requires `tsx` for TypeScript transpilation; works, but `tsx` may not be installed as a dependency in production — fine since it's in `devDependencies`.
- No `.nvmrc` file specifying Node 20; engines field exists but `nvm use` won't trigger automatically in CI.
- No `package.json` `private: true` enforcement on `@clinic/api` is missing; it IS set, good. But no `publishConfig` to prevent accidental publishing.
- The `apps/api/db/migrations/0001_init_bootstrap.sql` migration name lacks the numeric prefix that `node-pg-migrate` expects; the tool will not pick it up.
- The seed `01_minimum.ts` filename lacks a numeric prefix that some seed runners expect; `node-pg-migrate` runs migrations only, not seeds — so the seed script must be invoked separately, which it is, but there's no `node-pg-migrate seeds` plugin configured.
- The pino logger uses `timestamp: pino.stdTimeFunctions.isoTime` which produces ISO timestamps; fine. But the spec says logs carry `request_id`, `actor_role`, etc. as fields — these are top-level, which they are. However, `pino-http` adds `req`, `res` objects to the log line, which contain headers (including `x-auth-claim`!) — the redact list must cover `req.headers["x-auth-claim"]` or the entire claim will leak.
- `pino-http`'s default serializers will serialize `req.headers`; the `x-auth-claim` header contains the JSON-encoded `AuthClaim` with `branch_ids`. This is a PII leak vector even before E0-S3.
- The `apps/api/src/app.ts` does not register a 404 handler or a global not-found response; a request to `/unknown` returns Express's default HTML 404 page, which may expose stack details in development.
- The `apps/api/src/app.ts` error handler swallows the error stack — good for prod — but logs only the message (`err: message`); the spec says "no stack trace in response" (covered) but doesn't say "log the stack" — minor consistency.
- The CI workflow does not set `env:` to provide `DATABASE_URL` for the test step; the spec acceptance says "the test step does not require a live Postgres" but if any test ever accidentally touches the pool, it will fail confusingly.
- The CI workflow runs `pnpm -w build` after `pnpm -w test`; order matters for some monorepos; fine here.
- The CI workflow has no `if: success()` or `if: failure()` guards; standard hygiene.
- The CI workflow uses `ubuntu-latest` only; the architecture implies multi-region but CI matrix on `macos-latest` and `windows-latest` would catch OS-specific issues (e.g., `globalThis.crypto.randomUUID()` availability).
